title: Changing Environments
seo_title: Year 4 Science: Changing Environments Worksheets (Habitats, Pollution, Wildlife Surveys)
standard_code: Year 4: Living things and their habitats
standard_text: Recognise that environments can change and that this can sometimes pose dangers to living things.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 science worksheets on changing environments: natural and human changes, effects on habitats, seasons, hibernation and migration, and wildlife survey data. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Environments change; living things are affected.
key_sub: Some changes harm habitats, others protect them.
body_html:
How to think about it

Environments change, and this can help or harm living things.

  • Natural changes: seasons, floods, storms, droughts. Changes caused by people: building, pollution, litter, cutting down trees.
  • People can also improve habitats: nature reserves, ponds, hedgerows, bird boxes, wildflowers.
  • Living things cope with seasons by hibernating, migrating or losing leaves. Surveys over many years show trends.
Example

A pond is filled in. Effect?

Pond animals lose their habitat

Answer: frogs and newts must move or die

Example

Counts 50, 44, 38, 32. Trend?

Each count is lower

Answer: going down

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all changes are caused by people.
  • Thinking all changes harm wildlife.
  • Using one year's count to show a trend.

faq.a: Naturally, through seasons, floods, storms and droughts, and because of people, through building, pollution, litter and cutting down trees.

faq.q: How can changes be dangerous to living things?
faq.a: Animals and plants can lose their food, water or shelter, be poisoned by pollution, or be killed by traffic.
By creating nature reserves, ponds and hedgerows, planting wildflowers, putting up bird boxes and not dropping litter.

items.q: What is hibernation?
c: a deep sleep through winter to save energy
items.e: Hedgehogs hibernate.

items.q: Can environments change naturally?
c: Yes, for example through seasons, floods and storms.
items.e: Natural changes happen all the time.

items.q: What is an environment?
c: the surroundings and conditions where a living thing lives
items.e: Includes air, water, soil and other living things.

items.q: What is migration?
c: travelling to a different place for part of the year
items.e: Swallows migrate to Africa.

items.q: What is a nature reserve?
c: a protected area where wildlife is looked after
items.e: Protects habitats.

items.q: Trees in a rainforest are cut down. What is the most likely effect on living things?
c: Seabirds and turtles can swallow it or get tangled.
Algae grow fast and fish can die from lack of oxygen.
More bees and butterflies can find nectar.
Animals such as orangutans lose their homes and food.
items.e: Changes to a habitat change what can live there.
